Tonight it has forty-one verses; the new one is about a student who fell into the cellar.|The ballad has a verse about the castle now, and the regulars look at you when they reach it.} {The landlady pretends to hate it.|The whole room bangs time on the tables.|{season == "winter": Snow is coming down outside, and nobody is going anywhere.|The fire flares at the chorus, every time.}} Stand up and add a verse {You make up a verse about the landlady's slate and the room roars. She pours you a cider on the house, scowling.|You rhyme "Newt" with "absolute" and the whole tavern sings it back. You'll hear it for weeks.|Your verse about the castle gets a chorus of its own. The old regular claps you on the back and says you'll go in the ballad.} {You stand up, open your mouth and forget every word in the language. The old regular finishes your verse for you, kindly, and badly.|Your rhyme for "Newt" is "Newt". The room is silent, then merciless.|You sing your verse to the wrong tune. Half the room follows you and half the right one, and it ends in a brawl of harmonies.} Buy the singer a drink {You buy the old regular a cider, and he tells you the verses that aren't allowed in the ballad any more. They're the best ones.|You buy him a drink between verses. He toasts you in verse forty-two, which is new.|You buy the singer his usual. He tells you which verses are true. It's fewer than you'd hoped.}
